utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-96-23/2-I, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Zelenovic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. For the Prosecution Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, and I am again accompanied by case manager, Verica Balikic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Tjarda Van der Spoel, duty counsel for Mr. Zelenovic. And at Chamber's request, the chosen Defence counsel, Ognjanovic, who has not yet been assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. The purpose of this hearing is to hear a plea entered by Mr. Zelenovic. Mr. Zelenovic, did you have an opportunity discuss the indictment with counsel? And when I'm saying "counsel" I mean Mr. Ognjanovic who is in -- who is about, as I understand, about to be assigned as permanent counsel. Did you have an opportunity to discuss it with him?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have, Your Honour, yesterday in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday. I take it that you've received a copy of the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ognjanovic, I do understand that Mr. Zelenovic discussed with you the indictment. Have you received the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday morning, and we passed through the indictment -- yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you received it yesterday morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll come back to that later. Have you got any impression of the supporting material?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I received also on a CD with the supporting material and I passed through it last evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that is after you discussed the matters with Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that cause you any further need to speak with Mr. Zelenovic about a plea to be entered or --

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, there is no need for any further consultations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ognjanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Zelenovic, the whole of the indictment could be read to you. We also could proceed on the basis of the counts of the indictment to be read to you and that you then enter a plea on each of these counts. Do you insist on reading the whole of the indictment or would you be satisfied if I just put the separate counts to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I read it through with my Defence counsel yesterday, and there is no need to read it out in its entirety today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'll go through the indictment by reading out the counts, and invite you at -- at each of these counts to enter a plea. And these pleas will then be recorded. I first take you to Counts 5 to 8 of the indictment. Counts 5 to 8 of the indictment deal with what is briefly described in the heading as torture and rape at Buk Bijela. Count 5, you're charged with torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(F) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Zelenovic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the plea of not guilty in Count 5 should be recorded. Count 6, rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(G) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the not guilty on Count 6 should be recorded. Count 7, torture, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by common Article 3(1)(a), torture, of the Geneva Conventions. Mr. Zelenovic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the not guilty on Count 7 should be recorded. Count 8, rape, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. How plead, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The not guilty plea on Count 8 should be recorded. We then move on to Counts 13 to 16 of the indictment, torture and rape at Foca high school. Count 13, torture, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the not guilty plea on Count 13 should be recorded. Count 14, rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(G) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the not guilty plea on Count 14 should be recorded. Mr. Zelenovic, under Count 15 you're charged with torture, a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Common Article 3(a)(1), torture, of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The not guilty plea on Count 15 should be recorded. Count 16 charges you, Mr. Zelenovic, with rape, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The not guilty plea of Count 16 should be recorded, Mr. Registrar. I then on to Counts 41 to 44 which we find under the heading "torture and rape of women at partisan sports hall," five mentioned by pseudonyms but other women also included. Under Count 41, Mr. Zelenovic, you are charged with torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(F) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The not guilty plea on Count 41 should be recorded, Mr. Registrar. Count 42 charges you, Mr. Zelenovic, with rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(G) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, your plea on Count 42 is not heard by the interpreters and is not on the record. Could you please repeat your plea under Count 42 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty. Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The not guilty plea on Count 42 should be recorded, Mr. Registrar. Then Count 43, torture, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Common Article 3(a)(1), torture, of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The not guilty plea on Count 43 will be recorded. Count 44, rape, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The not guilty plea on Count 44 will be recorded. Then I finally take you to the last two counts of the indictment. They appear under the heading of rape of, and then two women are mentioned by their pseudonym and two other women. The women were taken from Karaman's house in Foca and were continued to be detained in different houses and apartments and continued to be subjected to sexual assaults. In Count 49 you're charged, Mr. Zelenovic, with rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(G) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead? We didn't hear a plea yet from you, Mr. Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The not guilty plea on that Count 49 will be recorded. Then the last count, Count 50, charges you, Mr. Zelenovic, with rape, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, the not guilty plea under Count 50 should be recorded. You've now entered your plea, Mr. Zelenovic. You showed yesterday already that you're aware that there is a request pending for your case to be referred to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Therefore, we have two proceedings going on at the same time, at this moment at least. And that is the charges brought against you before this Tribunal and at the same time the request for referral of the case to a domestic court in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Yesterday I asked you whether there were any other issues to be raised in -- related to detention or health. May I take it that the situation has not changed since yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then is there any other issue to be raised. Mr. Van der Spoel, did you have an opportunity to speak with Mr. Ognjanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I did. I met him at yesterday afternoon at 1.00. I talked about the appearance yesterday morning and your instructions, your observations. I informed him about those. Yesterday evening I also spoke to him and this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this cause you to raise any further issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour. Then, Mr. Ognjanovic, may I ask you, since approximately 30 days you were aware that Mr. Zelenovic would like to be assisted by you. I take it that you know the rules, so that you knew that within the next 30 days Mr. Zelenovic would have to enter a plea. Nevertheless, yesterday I had to establish, at least that's what Mr. Zelenovic told me, that apart from a short telephone conversation, that he had had no telephone contact with you, that's one. Two, I do understand that yesterday, for unknown reasons to me, you're not able to attend. I did not hear anything about you contacting either OLAD or the Registry to ask for a further delay or to speak with those responsible with how to proceed. That's two. Three, I do understand that it was yesterday only after you met with Mr. Zelenovic that you acquainted yourself with the supporting material, at least I take it the non-confidential part of it. I have not heard of any contact between you and the Prosecutor. It highly surprised me. Could you please explain to me why we had to sit here yesterday when you thought that your travelling schedule could be such that you would not be present in this court, and that you had not spoke with Mr. Zelenovic, that you had not had thorough contact with Mr. Van der Spoel, and that you had not had thorough contact with the Prosecution under the present circumstances. Would you please explain what made you choose this, may I say, surprising and extraordinary course of action?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this course of action was not actually a matter of my decision; it was by dint of circumstance that I had to take it. I was not informed 30 days ago about the fact that the accused wanted me to be his chosen counsel. This actually happened within the past two weeks. Over the two past weeks, I have had -- I have maintained constant contact with people from the Registry, Martin Petrov, and Ms. Reinhardt. In that interval, I had three or four telephone conversations with the accused in the Detention Unit, just these two or three or four very brief conversations, and they concern the exchange of information, and that is what we did. Finally, the day before yesterday I was informed in Belgrade that his initial appearance, the one for yesterday, would possibly be postponed for today, and that is why I set out on my journey yesterday because I thought it would be today. Then we talked on the telephone, and I advised him as to the way in which he should enter his plea in respect of the counts he is charged with. I came to The Hague only yesterday. I saw, I met, I had meetings with all the people here. I left all my telephone numbers with them and was -- and hoped that I would be contacted. But I could not establish -- get in touch with the Prosecution yesterday because I had to go to the Detention Unit. So it is not a matter of attitude in the sense of procrastination or dragging my feet, it is just something which so happened by dint of circumstance. It is not a matter of my wanting it to be that way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when did you for the first time make contact with Mr. Van der Spoel, who would be of course the first one to approach, since he was in charge of Defence duties?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, it was yesterday morning when I was in Germany.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not two weeks ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Because I didn't have any -- any detail or any phone number or any information about my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ask the OLAD for the -- for those details?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did they give you the phone number for Mr. Van der Spoel?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I received his name and his family name two days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you immediately phoned him, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: I tried -- I tried. It was day before yesterday, but for the first time we hear each other and had a phone contact yesterday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's not spend too much time on it, Mr. Ognjanovic. This Tribunal expects you to take an active attitude in whatever happens before this Tribunal. And I am, to be quite honest, a bit surprised that you learned only two weeks ago about the preference expressed by Mr. Zelenovic to be assisted by you. I'll verify this with the Registry why you were not informed at an earlier stage about this and to give me more details. Mr. Ognjanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- The Chamber did not much appreciate the course of events until now. We have discussed it. It's not my habit to go over matters a hundred times again, but please be aware of the position the Chamber takes in this respect. Is there any matter you would further like to raise? I know that you are not counsel yet, but if there would be anything that you would like to be discussed, please tell me, then I'll -- I'll give you an opportunity to communicate with Mr. Van der Spoel to see how we would proceed. Is there anything you would like to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: There is not any further issues except I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to visit my client, if it is possible, today afternoon in UNDU.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Judges are not masters of the schedule of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the visiting schedule, but of course I take it that Mr. Van der Spoel will give you the guidance you need to -- to visit your client as soon as possible. Mr. Ognjanovic, you are aware of time-limits set for preliminary motions?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, if you would like to file them, they should be filed by -- by when?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGNJANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe I'll do it in the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's not an answer to my question, but let's leave it as it is. We stand adjourned, and I announce that I do not know whether the next hearing will be a hearing of Trial Chamber I or whether you'll hear in between from the Referral Bench. And, Mr. Ognjanovic, as soon as you've taken over responsibilities, please keep in mind that you are playing chess on two boards at this moment and that you should keep a close eye on time-limits, both in the referral case and in this case which is pending before Trial Chamber I. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: adjourned at 8.28 a.m.
